durable JetStream internalizes a chunked async ack window whose chunk size IS the client's MaxPending of 64 with the acks joined between chunks, so a chunk starting from an empty window can never stall inside one call (PublishAsync takes no ctx and parks up to 200ms once the window is full, which is why that is one constant and not two), while Loopback and core NATS simply loop: the point of the batch is that no global contract may encode ONE adapter's delivery-guarantee latency, and a keep whose publish landed but whose ack was lost retries as a duplicate the decided set absorbs - the same ambiguity a failed synchronous publish always had; the flusher batches by OCCUPANCY and never by timer (one blocking receive plus a non-blocking gather of the queue - never a wait; size 1 at idle is byte-for-byte the old path by construction rather than by tuning, steady state is arrival rate x ack RTT), publish-before-consume is a batch BARRIER because other clusters' retention windows are burning, a failed keep's job skips its consume and re-parks BOTH bits with the ORIGINAL deadline, it is still ONE goroutine (ADR-009 r2's single emission point intact, census unchanged) with the publish join bounded by the stop signal through a channel-backed context TYPE rather than a watcher goroutine, and publishedKeeps/publishErrors now count per KEEP and not per call (identical at batch size 1, different above it - any alert reading publishErrors as a call count is reading a different number);
